input_text: On the issue of which of the defendants was responsible for driving the get-away car, the fact that the witness on the stand turned and pointed to the man in the blue suit.

extraction.input_text: On the issue of which of the defendants was responsible for driving the get-away car, the fact that the witness on the stand turned and pointed to the man in the blue suit.

claim.text: Is the statement described in this narrative hearsay under FRE 801(c)?

arguments.text: The witness's pointing occurred while testifying on the stand, constituting an in-court demonstration rather than an out-of-court statement.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) limits hearsay to out-of-court statements; in-court testimony or demonstrations are not hearsay.
arguments.evidence_span: the witness on the stand turned and pointed

arguments.text: Pointing is typically classified as non-assertive conduct rather than an assertion. Under FRE 801(a)(2), conduct only qualifies as a statement if the actor intended it as an assertion.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(a)(2) defines statements by conduct; non-assertive conduct falls outside the hearsay definition.
arguments.evidence_span: turned and pointed to the man in the blue suit

arguments.text: The evidence is offered to allow the jury to observe the witness's identification process and assess credibility in real time, rather than to prove the truth of a prior out-of-court assertion.
arguments.legal_rule: FRE 801(c) requires the statement to be offered to prove the truth of the matter asserted; in-court demonstrations serve a different evidentiary purpose.
arguments.evidence_span: On the issue of which of the defendants was responsible for driving the get-away car
